attacker_pocs.name: rsrc_named_string_overread
attacker_pocs.why: FT_New_Memory_Face on a PE .FON whose resource root has one named entry. The entry count sum is 1, so the old 16-bit loop never wraps. The new named-string check compares the character count against name_avail<<1 (bytes shifted the wrong way), then allocates name_avail bytes and FT_STREAM_READs name_chars*2 bytes. With a declared section raw size of 28 and a 4-character UTF-16 name that is fully present in the file, that is a 2-byte heap buffer and an 8-byte copy. Parent rejects the non-directory entry via the stream API and does not allocate.

role_a_rationale: The 16-bit resource-directory walk in fnt_face_get_dll_font is fixed by summing number_of_named_entries and number_of_id_entries in FT_ULong, rejecting totals above 0xFFFF, and iterating with a wide index at the root, name, and language levels, so a sum of 0x10000 no longer spins. A normal PE .FON with a single RT_FONT id entry still loads. The new code that validates a named entry's length-prefixed UTF-16 string uses a reversed shift in the section bound (nchars > avail<<1 instead of avail>>1) and then copies nchars*2 bytes into an allocation of only the remaining section bytes, which is a heap-buffer-overflow on a short declared section whose file still holds the string. That input does not overflow on the parent.
